diagnoses.label: silence smoothing window misaligned to timestamps
diagnoses.observable_evidence: silence-detector/scripts/detect_silence.py uses np.convolve(..., mode="valid") then sets silence_end=i directly from the smoothed index; with smoothing_window=30, smoothed[0] corresponds to original energy window [0..29], so returning i underestimates the true time by ~smoothing_window-1 (or requires a defined center/edge convention). SKILL.md describes smoothing but does not specify the timestamp mapping, and video-processor pipeline depends on this boundary to start pause detection.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: timestamp alignment for smoothed energy windows
diagnoses.scope_boundary: initial-silence end-time computation when smoothing is applied (moving average) and the returned boundary is used as a real timestamp for downstream segmenting
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: pause-detector local_avg computation (uniform_filter1d) which preserves array length and index-to-second mapping; also do not change energy-calculator windowing semantics
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Define and implement a consistent mapping from smoothed index to original-second timestamp (e.g., use 'same' convolution or add an explicit offset such as i + (smoothing_window-1) or i + (smoothing_window//2) depending on chosen convention), and document that convention in silence-detector/SKILL.md so downstream start-time usage is correct.

diagnoses.label: video-processor docs misroute report responsibility and pipeline call semantics
diagnoses.observable_evidence: video-processor/SKILL.md states it "Creates the processed video and a report JSON" and shows an internal report format with keys original_duration/output_duration, but the task requires compression_report.json with different keys and a segments_removed list. A separate report-generator skill exists that matches the task format, and the location hint requests checking video-processor/SKILL.md calling说明. This mismatch can cause users to rely on the wrong report artifact and wrong schema.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: artifact contract & schema routing (which component produces which report)
diagnoses.scope_boundary: documentation and expected outputs for end-to-end video-silence-remover pipeline, especially which report to deliver and which schema to follow
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: the internal process_video.py behavior of producing its own *_report.json (may remain as an auxiliary debug artifact); also do not alter report-generator schema which already matches the task
diagnoses.target_section: Output / Notes / Mandatory end-to-end completion gate references to report generation
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Clarify that the task-format compression_report.json must be generated via report-generator using original+compressed+final segments, and treat video-processor's *_report.json as optional internal stats; update the documented pipeline call sequence to pass the corrected silence boundary into pause detection and then into segment-combiner/video-processor.

diagnoses.label: silence-detector docs omit smoothing-to-time convention used by downstream start-time
diagnoses.observable_evidence: silence-detector/SKILL.md describes "Apply smoothing with moving average" and "Find where smoothed energy exceeds baseline x multiplier" but does not specify whether the returned end time corresponds to the start, center, or end of the smoothing window. Yet video-processor/SKILL.md mandates: "start long-pause detection at that returned boundary," making the boundary semantics critical.
diagnoses.mechanism_anchor: inter-skill contract for boundary semantics (start-time meaning)
diagnoses.scope_boundary: handoff of silence_end from silence-detector to pause-detector --start-time and to segment lists used for removal
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: segment-combiner merge rules or report-generator duration math; this is specifically about boundary semantics and documentation
diagnoses.target_section: How It Works / Notes (definition of returned silence end timestamp)
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Add an explicit definition of what timestamp the detector returns when smoothing is enabled (e.g., end-of-window or center-of-window), and ensure the JSON segment end and recommended pause-detector --start-time use that same convention.

overlay.primary_anchor: timestamp alignment for smoothed energy windows
overlay.composition_issue: The silence-detector returns a boundary derived from a length-reducing smoothing operation without a defined index-to-time mapping; video-processor documentation then instructs using that boundary as an absolute second for pause detection. This compounds into systematic misplacement of the opening cut and mis-starting pause detection, which can cascade into wrong segments_removed and report inconsistencies.
preservation_constraints: Preserve pause-detector local dynamic threshold behavior and its inclusive min_duration semantics
Preserve segment-combiner rule to not merge across positive gaps (only overlap/touch)
Preserve report-generator output schema and ffprobe-based duration measurement
Preserve video-processor ability to accept multiple remove-segments JSON inputs and produce a processed mp4

package_assessment.rationale: The defect is localized to a deterministic timestamp-mapping bug/omission in silence-detector smoothing and to documentation-level routing/contract issues in SKILL.md files. Fixing the mapping and clarifying the inter-skill boundary semantics should reliably correct downstream segment start-times without requiring changes to external tools or the end task.
